summary.text: Mark Klicker is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 16-Position 1, in office since January 11, 2021, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Kyle Palmer.
A Walla Walla native, he has farmed and worked in agriculture for more than 35 years.

paragraphs.text: Klicker grew up on his family's farm in the Walla Walla Valley, where his ancestors settled in 1861, according to his House Republican biography.
He was a regional field director for the Washington Farm Bureau from 1997 to 2012, then worked in farm and ranch real estate.

He raised cherries on the lower Snake River from 1991 to 2015, then became project coordinator for Monson Fruit Company on the same farm, and he now owns and operates Urban, Farm and Forest Group, a timber and forest management company.
Klicker was elected in 2020 to succeed Republican Bill Jenkin, who did not seek re-election, and defeated Democrat Frances Chvatal.
His biography says he is ranking member of the Local Government Committee, assistant ranking member of the Environment and Energy Committee, and a member of the Rules and Transportation committees.
It also says he wants to reduce taxes and promote and reward innovation.
